findings.title: The required installer acceptance test deletes a developer's pre-existing files in the repo it runs in (rm -rf of CLAUDE.local.md, .mcp.json, apps/api/CLAUDE.md, .vscode/): the 'Secondary' part of F-DG1-118 was not repaired
findings.reproduction: tools/deps/tests/install-sandbox.test.sh:139 `for p in CLAUDE.local.md .mcp.json apps/api/CLAUDE.md .vscode; do rm -rf "$ROOT/$p" 2>/dev/null; done` runs on the HOST (outside the sandbox) against ROOT = the repository containing the test, unconditionally, whether or not the test created those paths; line 124 likewise mv's "$ROOT/tools.mth-ac7" onto "$ROOT/tools". Neither file changed in this round (git diff 5204179..016433d touches only the AC-9 block). Disposable clone 016433d (log 17-test-cleanup-deletes-dev-files.log): seed .vscode/settings.json, CLAUDE.local.md, .mcp.json, apps/api/CLAUDE.md -> `bash tools/deps/tests/install-sandbox.test.sh` -> all four are gone afterwards. The orchestrator runs this test in the real repository as a required DG1 check, so a developer's untracked editor/agent configuration there is irrecoverably deleted.
findings.expected: As stated in F-DG1-118's expected outcome: the acceptance test must not rm -rf/mv pre-existing paths of the real repo. E.g. run AC-7/AC-8 against a disposable copy (--root <scratch>) or record which paths existed before and remove only what the probe itself created.
findings.actual: Pre-existing CLAUDE.local.md, .mcp.json, apps/api/CLAUDE.md and .vscode/ are deleted by every run of the test.

history.note: Raised by code-security-reviewer in DG1 round 4; reproduced in a disposable clone. Split out of F-DG1-118 (whose primary escape is CLOSED_VERIFIED) so its severity is tracked honestly.

findings.title: install-sandbox.sh copy-back hardening: copy errors are ignored (installer exits 0 after a failed/partial cp), and the destination set is 'any package.json at depth <= 4 on disk' rather than the pnpm-workspace.yaml members its comment claims
findings.reproduction: Static, tools/deps/install-sandbox.sh @016433d. (a) Lines 150-151 `rm -rf "$dest"; cp -a "$wsnm" "$dest"` have no error check and line 155 is an unconditional `exit 0`: if cp fails (ENOSPC from a dependency that fills the disposable copy, I/O error), the real member's node_modules has already been deleted or is partial and the installer still reports success. F-DG1-118's expected outcome asked to 'fail (non-zero) on any copy error'. A dynamic attempt (an unreadable directory planted in node_modules) was stopped earlier by pnpm itself (EACCES, exit 243), so this part is not reproduced dynamically. (b) Line 153 enumerates `find "$REPO_ROOT" -maxdepth 4 -name package.json -not -path '*/node_modules/*'` on the real FILESYSTEM (tracked and untracked), while the comment (lines 138-143) says 'the root and every committed package.json directory' and pnpm-workspace.yaml declares only apps/* and packages/*. Today the two sets are identical (8 paths, verified), so there is no current exploit; but any future package.json at depth <= 4 outside the workspace (e.g. a test fixture such as tools/gates/fixtures/package.json, or an untracked one) silently becomes a copy-back destination where dependency code can plant a node_modules that scripts in that directory would resolve.
findings.expected: Fail non-zero on any rm/cp error in the copy-back; derive the destinations from pnpm-workspace.yaml globs (plus the root) resolved on the real tree, or from `git ls-files` package.json entries, matching the documented contract.
findings.actual: cp failures are swallowed; destinations follow the on-disk package.json set.

findings.title: The module dependency-lint still misses the Function/AsyncFunction constructor reached through a constructed (non-literal) key, e.g. f["constr" + "uctor"] or Reflect.get(f, "constr".concat("uctor")) (follow-on to F-DG1-121)
findings.reproduction: apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts @016433d: element access is checked only when literalText(key) === "constructor" (line ~187), and the string-value rule (lines ~233-242) only matches the literal "constructor". Plant (plant-f121.sh / plant-f121.test.ts, disposable clone, log 22-plant-f121.log): scanSource reports NO evasion for `f["constr" + "uctor"]`, `Reflect.get(fn, "constr".concat("uctor"))`, a template-literal key and an Object.getOwnPropertyNames(...).find(...) key; a real file apps/api/src/modules/access/zz-planted.ts using `const F = f["constr" + "uctor"]; F("s","return import(s)")("../transformations/routes.ts")` leaves architecture.test.ts green (54/54, exit 0). Runtime probe in Node 22.22.2 (23-f121-computed-key-runtime.log): the same form performs a dynamic import of another file ('internal-of-other-module').
findings.expected: The lint's documented claim ('the rules close every syntactic route') holds, or the residual is recorded: e.g. report element access with a non-literal key whose receiver is a function expression/identifier bound to a function, or ban Reflect.get/getOwnPropertyNames on functions in module code, or document constructed-key evaluation as an accepted residual of a static lint in ADR-0002.
findings.actual: A one-line constructed-key loader bypasses the module-interface check undetected.
